bc_warm_up_area.blurb: A small cluster of boulders in the Lower Left part of The Stacks, in the Fraser Valley near Hope. These are the first blocks you meet on the trail in, which makes them a natural place to loosen up. All 14 problems are bouldering, and the grades lean gentle: a handful of very easy lines and V0s, a couple of V1s and a V2, then a few V3s and a single V4. The names hint at cracks, an offwidth and an arete, so expect simple, honest movement rather than hard technical sequences. Good for beginners, kids, or anyone building up before the harder problems nearby.

bc_shannon_springs_wall.blurb: A fairly new crag tucked beside Shannon Falls near Squamish, close enough that you can hear the water. It holds 14 routes, mostly trad with a few sport lines, on grippy, featured stone with slabby crack and face climbing. Grades run from around 5.5 up to 5.10, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, so it suits climbers stepping up in the grades as well as those wanting moderate leads. The base is flat and the setting is pleasantly shady. Bring a standard rack with extra small pieces and a 60 m rope.

bc_tidal_zawn.blurb: The first big cliff at Copper Cove, a seaside spot in West Vancouver near Horseshoe Bay. It is a sea-carved inlet with steep walls and slabby sections at the south end. Of 14 climbs, most are top-rope lines, with a few sport routes and one trad climb. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.11, with a cluster around 5.10. Only a few lines are properly bolted, so many climbers top-rope using natural anchors. Expect a breezy, exposed feel with waves below, and check the tide before heading down to the base.

bc_alpha_wall.blurb: A popular wall in Cougar Canyon, in the Okanagan near Vernon, a short way past Rocky Horror Wall. It has 14 routes, ten sport and four trad, on gneiss. Grades climb from 5.7 to 5.12, with the weight in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, which is why it is known for quality moderates. It faces south, so it is a good pick when you want warmth and sun. A solid choice for climbers working through the middle grades on well-bolted lines.

bc_beta_wall.blurb: One of the harder-leaning walls in Cougar Canyon, near Vernon in the Okanagan. It has 14 routes, ten sport and four trad, on gneiss. Climbs range from 5.8 to 5.12, but most sit in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, and the climbing is described as excellent. The routes are on the longer side for the canyon, the walk from the creek is short, and there is a comfortable spot at the base for belaying. A good destination for strong intermediates.
